task.request: Help me cut CI time. Use popup to work through the useful options with me.
task.context: We have already inspected the workflow. Four jobs each run the same 2-minute dependency install. The integration suite runs serially for 11 minutes because tests share a Postgres database. There is a Linux/macOS/Windows matrix; production runs Linux, but the CLI has supported users on all three. PRs currently run the complete matrix even for docs-only edits. Runner usage is billed by the minute. No flaky-test investigation or cache experiment has been run yet. I can accept some additional spend, but I haven't set a limit. Preserve release coverage unless I explicitly choose otherwise.
task.combined_intent: Combine dependency caching with isolated parallel integration tests; preserve platform coverage. Qualify the budget and isolation proposal where the interaction permits.
task.correction: Actually, start by measuring the install and integration timings on three representative PRs. Don't change coverage or spend yet.

elements.markdown: The inspected workflow repeats a 2-minute install in four jobs and runs the integration suite serially for 11 minutes against shared Postgres. Caching could reduce repeated setup; integration parallelism could shorten the longest supplied test phase, but only after database isolation is proven. Four installs account for 8 job-minutes of work, not necessarily 8 minutes of wall-clock delay. We have no cache experiment or flaky-test investigation yet.

I propose keeping Linux/macOS/Windows release coverage: the CLI has supported users on all three. Production being Linux does not establish that the other platforms are expendable. For PRs, docs-only filtering is a separate opportunity to avoid unnecessary runs while keeping code-change coverage. Runner billing means shorter elapsed time can still cost more if extra workers increase total minutes.

definition.submit: Submit CI investigation and change proposal

elements.markdown: Four jobs each repeat a 2-minute install: that is 8 runner-minutes per run, though jobs overlapping means less than 8 minutes of wall-clock savings. The serial integration suite takes 11 minutes and shares Postgres, so parallel execution needs isolation first. All three platforms have supported CLI users; I propose retaining their release coverage. Docs-only PRs currently pay for the complete matrix. Cache behavior, test reliability and an acceptable spend increase are still unmeasured.

elements.multi: Which improvements should we develop together?

options.description: Establish wall time, runner-minutes and failures before comparing changes.
Target repeated installs; actual savings depend on hit rates and cache overhead.
Target the 11-minute suite; isolation and worker costs need investigation.

options.value: Skip irrelevant checks on docs-only PRs
options.description: Avoid unnecessary matrix work while retaining release checks and validating path classification.
Explore PR coverage tradeoffs; supported CLI platforms make exclusions consequential.

Measure a baseline.input: Proposed baseline measurement — edit the sample
Measure a baseline.default: Measure three representative PRs using existing runner settings: per-job install and test times, total wall time, billed runner-minutes by platform, and failures or retries. Record commit and workload so later experiments are comparable.

Cache dependencies.input: Proposed cache experiment — edit the policy
Cache dependencies.default: Identify the package manager, then cache its download store keyed by OS, runtime version and lockfile hash. Keep the existing reproducible install. Compare a cold run and a warm run, including restore/save overhead and billed minutes, before adopting the cache.

Cache dependencies.select: Should the first experiment include fallback cache restores?

options.description: Simpler invalidation; lockfile changes remain cold until a new cache is saved.
May recover downloads after lockfile changes; adds validation and experiment work.

Compare fallback restores too.markdown: Restore only a compatible download store, then run the same reproducible install. Compare exact-hit, fallback-hit and cold runs; do not count a restored cache as proof of correct dependencies.

Compare fallback restores too.default: Adopt only if correctness checks pass and fallback restores reduce measured wall time or billed minutes enough to justify the extra policy.

Isolate and parallelize integration test.markdown: A shared database explains the current serial execution, but does not establish that separate databases are sufficient. Global fixtures, migrations, ports and cleanup may also be shared. More workers can reduce wall time while increasing billed minutes; no speedup or cost is established yet.

Isolate and parallelize integration test.select: How far should the isolation work go next?

options.description: Inspect shared state and test reliability before changing execution or runner usage.
Develop a small pilot, with execution gated on the spend decision below.

Investigate and return a proposal.default: Inspect fixture scope, database naming, migration assumptions, external shared resources and cleanup. Review existing failures without assuming flakiness. Return an isolation design, expected runner usage and a benchmark plan before altering execution.

Prepare an isolated two-worker experimen.default: Give each of two workers its own disposable Postgres database and connection URL, apply migrations per database, partition tests and clean up even on failure. Verify other shared resources are isolated. Compare serial and two-worker runs on the same workload for correctness, failures, wall time and billed minutes.

Prepare an isolated two-worker experimen.markdown: If inspection finds unsafe shared state, stop at the isolation proposal. A two-worker pilot is a benchmark candidate, not a promise of halving the 11-minute suite.

Skip irrelevant checks on docs-only PRs.input: Proposed docs-only policy — edit the boundaries
Skip irrelevant checks on docs-only PRs.default: Retain full release coverage on Linux, macOS and Windows. For PRs that touch only verified documentation paths, run documentation checks and satisfy required-check rules without launching the full code matrix. Treat workflow, dependency, generated-code and executable-example changes as code until inspected.

Skip irrelevant checks on docs-only PRs.markdown: Before implementing, inspect path dependencies and branch protection. Test the classification against representative docs-only and mixed PRs so a path filter cannot hide a required check or omit code affected by documentation tooling.

Propose representative PR checks plus full supported-platform checks before release, explaining which regressions would be detected later. Do not remove checks during this investigation.

Consider changing release coverage.placeholder: Which platform or support commitment could change, and why?

Consider changing release coverage.markdown: Production running Linux does not remove the CLI's macOS and Windows obligations. Assess affected users and the support policy, then return the exact coverage change for review before implementing it.

elements.markdown: For caching plus integration isolation, measure each change separately before combining them. Use the same workloads so cache savings do not conceal increased database setup or worker costs.
